principles.text: Your codebase, more than prompts or AGENTS.md, is the biggest influence on AI output, so keep it easy to change.
Prefer a few deep modules with simple interfaces: design the interface yourself and delegate the implementation.
Before implementing, have the agent grill you until you reach a shared understanding; agents can't read your mind.
Install brakes first: cheap checks, a separate reviewer agent, then human review. Speed without them is a slop cannon.
Ban `any` by default, and use generics, not `unknown`, to give utility functions exact types without casts.

sampleQA.question: How should I structure a codebase so AI coding agents work well in it?

answer.text: Treat the agent as a new starter with no memory. Your codebase shapes its output more than your prompts or AGENTS.md do.
Use a few deep modules with simple interfaces, not many shallow modules with big interfaces.
Treat them as grey boxes: you own the interface, AI owns the implementation, and tests keep it honest.
Don't cut a seam until something varies across it. A seam with a single adapter is just indirection.
Ban it by default with the ESLint rule, and use eslint-disable for the legitimate exceptions.
Use it in wide type argument constraints such as `any[]` parameters, because an `unknown` constraint rejects functions with real parameters.
When a generic function returns a conditional type, `as any` plus a unit test is often better, since TypeScript can't verify the return.
In utility functions, swapping `any` for `unknown` only moves the problem to consumers. Generics are the way out.

sampleQA.question: What should I do before an agent starts implementing a feature?

answer.text: Have it interview you relentlessly about the plan until you reach a shared understanding, rather than rushing to a plan.
Agree on names for concepts in a shared glossary, because agents thrive on consistent language.
Split the work into thin vertical slices sized for one session, so each one stays in the smart zone and gets feedback early.
Treat specs as temporary scheduling artifacts and delete them once the code lands.
